items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The 30th of March, 1945, I did a recording that gave me one of the greatest thrills of my life... the rest of the line was Buster Bailey, Benny Carter, John Kirby Oscar Moore, Nat 'King' Cole, Max Roach and a girl singer named Kay Starr.

ctx.x: We did at least three broadcasted live radio shows for the Armed Forces which were M.C'ed by Ernest Whitman, an actor whom I had seen many times at the Lafayette and Apollo Theatres and these shows were also recorded on V Disc. I heard quite a few V Disc later, but never one that the Kirby band did.

The 30th of March, 1945, I did a recording that gave me one of the greatest thrills of my life. Coleman Hawkins had come to Los Angeles and was working at Shepp's Playhouse on First Street, just around the corner from my hotel. He was engaged for the recording date and the rest of the line was Buster Bailey, Benny Carter, John Kirby Oscar Moore, Nat 'King' Cole, Max Roach and a girl singer named Kay Starr.

Al Hall had introduced me to Nat Cole a few years before, and also Oscar Moore, who was Nat's guitarist. They were playing at Kelly's Stable then, and had not become very well known. I had never heard of or met Max Roach, and Kay Starr was a west coast singer that I had not heard about also. We recorded four numbers, and one included "Stormy Weather", which Kay sang, and "If I Could Be With You One Hour Tonight". I had recorded with Benny before, and Coleman Hawkins in 1943, but this recording intrigued me more…
